newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-DRIVING SNOW FAILS TO STOP NORWAY.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-DRIVING SNOW FAILS TO STOP NORWAY.

text.p: Norway ignored driving snow to record an impressive win in the Nordic combined team event at the Nordic skiing world championships on Wednesday.

Fred Boerre Lundberg, who completed the last lap in the 4x5-km relay, crossed the line waving a Norwegian flag in a winning time of 52 minutes 18 seconds to hand the home team their third gold medal in the 10-day festival.
Finland and Austria, who finished second and third, never matched the Norwegians, who used the cross-country competition to increase the lead they had built in the morning's ski jumping.
Two brilliant jumps of 93.5 and 94 metres by Bjarte Engen Vik gave Norway a seven-second headstart in the relay over Finland and 15 seconds ahead of the Czech Republic.

A strong lap by Halldor Skard, the first Norwegian to set off in the relay, helped them improve their lead to nearly 30 seconds. The rest of the race was merely a formality for Skard's team mates Vik, Knut Tore Apeland and Lundberg.
As the Czechs soon dropped back, Finland fought a close battle for second place with Austria, who were fourth after the ski jumping.
The Finns took the silver medal, 45.6 second behind with Austria a further 27.5 seconds back in third place.

There was disappointment for World and Olympic champions Japan who were a modest sixth after the ski jumping, partly because of poor performances by Kenji Ogiwara, Sunday's individual world champion. They eventually finished ninth.
The Norwegians drew inspiration from Bjorn Daehlie who won his second gold medal in Tuesday's 15-km freestyle pursuit.
"He showed us the way," said Lundberg, the individual Olympic champion. "It's good to win with guys you know so well and like so much. We practically live together and we get on very well."
Another reason for the Norwegians' success was their preparation for bad weather.
"Our skis were waxed for snow," Skard said. "When it started to fall after the ski jumping, we knew immediately it would be good for us.
